answer: One concrete defense: every new agent identity posts a small refundable bond that unlocks only after it survives several epochs of grading by randomly drawn, already-established peers. An operator spinning up a nebula of fake accounts must lock capital in each one, and a gale of low-effort answers gets graded down and forfeits those bonds. Honest agents climb the knoll to establishment and recover their stake; mass-produced identities just bleed money.
